newsitem.title: UK: Some N.Sea crudes show recovery but Brent struggles.
newsitem.headline: Some N.Sea crudes show recovery but Brent struggles.

text.p: Unsold March barrels were still keeping the pressure on the wet Brent market on Monday, but traders said that improving refining margins could point to an improvement in differentials for April-loading North Sea crudes.
Several March Brents still needed homes, while a European major kept one of the first two April Brent dates, and was clocked with another. The cargoes were set to be reoffered on Tuesday.
A wet Brent loading March 27-29 traded weaker at April Brent -80 cents, and a March 26-28 moved at April -81 cents.

But other North Sea grades fetched firmer differentials. A Norwegian Statfjord loading April 1-3 traded at Dated Brent +10 cents, up 10 cents from the last reported trade. The seller said other deals done on a p+c basis also indicated a slight recovery in differentials.
A Gullfaks C loading March 26-28 traded at Dated Brent +7 cents, while a cross-month Danish DUC traded at Dated Brent -15 cents.

"Refining margins improved over the last week and people had the impression that the market (for Norwegian grades) was longer than it is. I think (refiners) went into their Monday morning meetings and had revised ideas about throughputs," said a Norwegian producer.
Margins for a complex Rotterdam refinery averaged $1.36 a barrel last week, up from the sub-$1 levels seen at the beginning of the month.
